healthTips.title: Health tips
healthTips.subtitle: Simple daily habits for a healthier life.

plate.title: Fill half your plate with vegetables
plate.body: Add dal, beans or eggs for protein and choose whole grains like brown rice, millets or whole-wheat roti.

fruit.title: Eat fruit instead of sweets
fruit.body: Two servings of seasonal fruit a day give fibre and vitamins with far less sugar than desserts or packaged snacks.

salt.title: Go easy on salt and fried food
salt.body: Too much salt raises blood pressure. Limit pickles, papad, namkeen and deep-fried snacks to occasional treats.

walk.title: Walk 30 minutes a day
walk.body: A brisk walk five days a week helps your heart, blood sugar and mood. Split it into three 10-minute walks if that is easier.

strength.title: Build strength twice a week
strength.body: Squats, push-ups against a wall or carrying bags of groceries keep muscles and bones strong as you age.

sitting.title: Break up long sitting
sitting.body: Stand up and move for a couple of minutes every hour, especially if you work at a desk or watch long hours of TV.

talk.title: Talk to someone you trust
talk.body: Sharing worries with family or friends lightens the load. If sadness lasts more than two weeks, speak to a doctor.

breathe.title: Try slow breathing when stressed
breathe.body: Breathe in for 4 seconds, hold for 4, breathe out for 6. A few minutes calms the body and mind.

screens.title: Take breaks from screens
screens.body: Put your phone away during meals and the hour before bed. Time outdoors and with people is good for your mind.

schedule.title: Keep a regular sleep time
schedule.body: Adults need 7–9 hours. Going to bed and waking up at the same time every day, even on weekends, improves sleep.

caffeine.title: Avoid tea and coffee late in the day
caffeine.body: Caffeine can keep you awake for hours. Try to have your last cup before 3 pm.

darkRoom.title: Make your room dark and quiet
darkRoom.body: A cool, dark room helps you fall asleep faster. Switch off bright lights and screens 30 minutes before bed.

water.title: Drink water through the day
water.body: Most adults need about 8 glasses a day, more in hot weather or when active. Pale yellow urine is a good sign.

heat.title: Protect yourself in hot weather
heat.body: Carry water, avoid the midday sun and wear light cotton clothes. Dizziness or confusion in heat needs urgent care.

ors.title: Use ORS for diarrhoea or vomiting
ors.body: Oral rehydration solution replaces lost salts and water. See a doctor if symptoms last more than a day or there is blood.

checkups.title: Get regular health check-ups
checkups.body: Check blood pressure, blood sugar and cholesterol every year after 30, or as your doctor advises.

vaccines.title: Keep vaccinations up to date
vaccines.body: Children need their full schedule, and adults may need tetanus, flu and other boosters. Ask your doctor what is due.

handwash.title: Wash your hands often
handwash.body: Wash with soap for 20 seconds before eating, after using the toilet and after coming home to prevent infections.

healthTips.disclaimer: General wellness information, not medical advice. Ask your doctor about your own health.

support.title: Help & support
support.subtitle: How to use the app, common questions and how to reach us.

describe.title: Describe your symptoms
describe.body: Tap the microphone or type what you feel, as in your own words.

answer.title: Answer a few questions
answer.body: The AI asks follow-up questions one at a time. Pick the answer that fits best.

review.title: Check your summary
review.body: See your symptoms, risk level and the recommended specialist. Save it as a PDF or share it.

doctor.title: Send it to a doctor
doctor.body: Choose a doctor and submit. Track the status in History.

prescription.title: Get your prescription
prescription.body: When the doctor approves it, open it from History or Prescriptions and download the PDF.

diagnosis.q: Is the AI result a diagnosis?
diagnosis.a: No. The AI helps organise your symptoms and suggests a risk level and specialist. Only a doctor can diagnose you or prescribe medicine.

emergency.q: What should I do in an emergency?
emergency.a: Do not wait for the app. Call 112 (emergency) or 108 (ambulance) straight away. The Emergency page has one-tap call buttons.

time.q: How long until a doctor reviews my case?
time.a: It depends on the doctor's availability. Your case shows "Pending review" in History until the doctor responds, then "Prescription ready".

privacy.q: Who can see my health information?
privacy.a: You and the doctor you send your case to. Signing out removes your health details from this device, so always sign out on a shared phone.

language.q: How do I change the language?
language.a: Open Profile and choose a language under Language. The app switches immediately.

pdf.q: How do I save my prescription as a PDF?
pdf.a: Open the prescription and tap Download PDF. If a direct download isn't available, your browser's print screen opens — choose "Save as PDF".

followUp.q: How do I book a follow-up?
followUp.a: Go to History, find the consultation and tap Book Follow-up, then pick a date and doctor.

otp.q: I didn't receive my OTP. What now?
otp.a: Wait a minute and check the number you entered, then tap Resend. Codes expire after 10 minutes, and 5 wrong attempts lock sign-in for 15 minutes.
